title: One 1962 Blast Moved 12 Million Tons of Earth in Seconds

scenes.text: One test blast moved twelve million tons of Earth.
In 1962, a 104 kiloton bomb went off underground in Nevada.
It left a crater 1,280 feet wide. That's wider than the Eiffel Tower is tall.
And 320 feet deep. A thirty-storey building could be buried inside.
It was an experiment, to see if nuclear blasts could dig canals and harbours.
The crater is still there today. Twelve million tons, from one blast.

description:
One 1962 test blast in Nevada moved about twelve million tons of Earth.
The Sedan crater is 1,280 feet wide and 320 feet deep.
Could you imagine digging a canal this way?
first_comment: Which is wilder: the 1,280-foot width or the 320-foot depth?
